Legacy campaign

Renew the Grid (2022–2041)

Which oil plants are still running after seven generations? It's 2022, and any you kept from 2000 or earlier will need to retire as California's demand grows.

Open the Legacy campaign↗ Your decisions ↓

Play the chapters in order. You carry the same utility from one generation to the next.

Location
A fictional California utility
Starts in
2022
Generation
20 years

Your starting point

When 2030 arrives, oil equipment that's at least thirty years old drops to 60% output. How much power you lose depends on what you built and kept in earlier terms.

By the end of year fourteen, you need to retire oil equipment commissioned in 2000 or earlier. Check the commissioning dates before you put in the first replacement order.

Learn how to play

Your decisions

  1. 01

    Find the units due to retire

    See how much power those units supply today. You may have already replaced some of them in an earlier chapter.

  2. 02

    Time the replacements

    Compare opening dates with the output cut in 2030 and the retirement deadline. Demand will keep growing while the fleet changes over.

  3. 03

    Decide what to pass on

    Check what the new equipment will cost customers and what it will emit. The last generation of your company will inherit those plants and any debt.

How much old oil capacity will you still depend on in 2030?
